# VALE3.SA: Technical Analysis for a 4-Week Relative-Return Horizon (as of 2026-07-06)

## Scope and data notes

- **Price data:** 126 daily bars from 2026-01-02 to 2026-07-06. The Dividends column is 0.0 on every row, so this window shows no dividend adjustments. I can't confirm the dividend-adjusted series from this data.
- **Verified snapshot:** The latest row is 2026-07-06: Open 76.1531, High 76.6297, Low 75.3847, Close 75.6667, Volume 12,389,100 (vs. a 20-session average of 17,108,760). The snapshot is the source of truth. The indicator values from the individual tool calls for 2026-07-06 (10 EMA 76.36, 50 SMA 78.72, 200 SMA 72.40, RSI 41.68, Bollinger middle 76.89, ATR 1.70, MACD -0.883) match it. I found no discrepancies.
- **Not covered:** Fundamentals, iron ore prices, news, and the ex-dividend calendar. These can dominate VALE3 over a 4-week window, so the technical read below is incomplete.
- **Horizon:** Entry at the first close after 2026-07-06 (i.e., the 2026-07-07 close), exit 20 sessions later. The target is VALE3's total return minus ^BVSP's return.

## Indicators selected (8, no redundancy)

| Indicator | Role in this analysis |
|---|---|
| close_200_sma | Long-term trend anchor |
| close_50_sma | Intermediate trend and dynamic resistance |
| close_10_ema | Short-term momentum and reclaim level |
| macd | Momentum direction and zero-line regime |
| rsi | Momentum strength and oversold/overbought context |
| boll | Mean-reversion reference (20 SMA) |
| atr | Volatility sizing for stops and expected move |
| vwma | Volume-weighted price level, used to check whether volume supports the moves |

I did not pull macds or macdh separately; the verified snapshot gives the signal line (-0.873) and histogram (-0.011) for the latest row.

## Trend structure

**Long-term: still constructive.** The price (75.67) is about 4.5% above the 200 SMA (72.40). The 200 SMA has risen steadily from 66.58 (2026-05-07) to 72.40, roughly 0.12–0.15 points per session. A rising 200 SMA with price above it means the broader uptrend that began in early 2026 has not broken.

**Intermediate: deteriorating.** The 50 SMA has fallen from 80.52 (2026-05-07) to 78.72, and the price sits about 3.9% below it. The 50 SMA is now sloping down, so it is acting as resistance rather than support. This is the main reason the setup is less constructive than the long-term picture.

**Short-term: weak.** The price is below the 10 EMA (76.36, about 0.9% below), and the 10 EMA has been flat to slightly down since 2026-06-22 (78.21). It was rolling over from 80.9 in early June.

**Path of the year.** VALE3 peaked near 87.6 (2026-02-11 close). It then fell to about 76 in March, traded in a roughly 75–82 range from April through June, and is now at the bottom of that range. The closes on 2026-06-10 (75.58), 2026-06-24 (75.61), and today (75.67) cluster in the same area. I'm noting this as a reference zone based on closes only; I have not verified that it has held as support in the past.

## Momentum

**MACD: bearish regime, flattening.** The MACD line crossed from positive to negative in early June. It was +0.10 on 2026-06-02, fell to -1.11 on 2026-06-12, and is -0.88 today. The histogram is -0.011, almost zero, so bearish momentum is fading but has not reversed. A MACD move back above zero would be the first meaningful sign of trend repair. Note that the MACD line sits just above its signal line at the moment only in the sense that the histogram is negative and shrinking. The verified values put MACD at -0.883 and the signal at -0.873, so the line is slightly below its signal.

**RSI: neutral-to-weak, not oversold.** RSI is 41.7. It bounced from 37.96 (2026-06-10) to 49.33 (2026-06-22), then fell back. RSI has not reached the 30 threshold in this window, so there is no oversold reading. The failed push toward 50 in late June is consistent with sellers still controlling rallies.

## Volatility and bands

**Bollinger Bands:** The middle band is 76.89 (price is 1.6% below it), the upper band 79.27, and the lower band 74.50. The price is in the lower half of the bands, with the 10 EMA and Bollinger middle as overhead reference points. The bands have narrowed from a wider configuration in mid-June, so volatility is compressing.

**ATR: volatility is contracting.** ATR is 1.70, down from a peak of about 2.20 (2026-06-05). That is roughly 2.2% of the current price per day. A stop at 1 ATR below entry would be about 74.0; at 2 ATR, about 72.3, which is close to the 200 SMA. These are sizing references, not recommendations.

**Rough move scale:** If daily ranges persisted at the current ATR, a 20-session window would have a natural spread on the order of ±7–8 points. This is a crude scaling, not a forecast. It is useful mainly to show that an index-relative outcome of a few percent is well within normal noise for this stock.

## Volume

**VWMA: price is slightly below the volume-weighted average.** VWMA is 76.84, and the price is about 1.5% below it. The VWMA has been falling since early June (from 80.46 on 2026-06-01), which tracks the price decline.

**Today's volume is light on a down day.** The stock fell 1.33% on 2026-07-06 (from 76.69 to 75.67) on 12.4M shares, roughly 72% of the 20-session average. Light-volume declines are less concerning than heavy-volume breakdowns, but they also don't show capitulation. The lower volume on the 2026-07-03 bar (7.8M) was in a holiday-shortened session and shouldn't be over-read.

## Relative strength versus ^BVSP (verified snapshot)

| Window | VALE3.SA | ^BVSP | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 sessions | -0.44% | -0.44% | 0.00% |
| 20 sessions | -0.36% | +2.24% | -2.60% |
| 60 sessions | -9.11% | -10.28% | +1.16% |
| 120 sessions | +4.11% | +5.56% | -1.45% |

- VALE3 has underperformed the index over the last 20 sessions by 2.6 points, which is the most recent relative weakness.
- Over 60 sessions it outperformed slightly, which suggests the earlier weakness (March–April) was the bigger drag.
- Beta is 0.99 and correlation 0.62 over 120 sessions. The stock tracks the index closely, so the relative outcome over the next 4 weeks will depend largely on stock-specific drivers (commodity and company news) that these tools cannot see.

## Synthesis for the 4-week horizon

**Overall tilt: neutral to slightly bearish on a relative basis.** The long-term trend is intact, but the intermediate and short-term structure is weakening. The MACD is below zero, the 50 SMA is falling and overhead, and the price is below both the 10 EMA and the Bollinger middle. The 20-session relative performance is negative. Momentum is fading rather than strongly negative. RSI is not oversold, so the setup doesn't yet offer a clean mean-reversion entry.

**Bullish case (would need confirmation):**
- A close back above the 10 EMA (76.36) and Bollinger middle (76.89), with volume above average.
- MACD crossing back above zero or the histogram turning positive.
- RSI reclaiming 50 and holding it.
- Invalidation of the bearish case would be a close above the 50 SMA (78.72), which would be the first sign of intermediate trend repair.

**Bearish case:**
- A daily close below the recent cluster near 75.6, with rising volume, opens a move toward the lower Bollinger band (74.50) and then the 200 SMA (72.40). The 200 SMA is rising, so it may provide support, but I can't verify that from the data.
- MACD falling further below its signal line, and RSI falling below 40, would confirm.

**Practical framing for the call:** The best-supported read is that VALE3 lacks a confirmed directional edge against the index for the next 4 weeks. The trade-off is between entering early at a level with limited confirmation and waiting for a reclaim of the 10 EMA or 50 SMA. Any position should be sized to the ATR (~1.7 points per day). Because the outcome is measured relative to ^BVSP, a view on VALE3 alone is not enough. The trader also needs a view on the stock's specific drivers versus the index. That is outside the scope of these technical tools.

**Key caveats:** The dividend-adjusted series is not visible here. The analysis excludes fundamentals and news. The reference levels above are based on observed closes, not on verified past support tests.

---

## Summary table

| Area | Observation | Evidence (verified) | Implication for 4-week relative call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Last close | 75.67 on 2026-07-06 | Snapshot | Entry reference is the 2026-07-07 close |
| Long-term trend | Constructive | Price 4.5% above rising 200 SMA (72.40) | Supports the long-term base |
| Intermediate trend | Weakening | 50 SMA falling from 80.52 to 78.72; price 3.9% below | 50 SMA is overhead resistance |
| Short-term trend | Weak | Price below 10 EMA (76.36) | Needs a reclaim for a constructive signal |
| MACD | Bearish, flattening | MACD -0.883, signal -0.873, histogram -0.011 | Watch for zero-line crossover |
| RSI | Neutral-weak | 41.68; low of 37.96 on 2026-06-10 | Not oversold; no mean-reversion trigger |
| Bollinger Bands | Lower-half position | Middle 76.89; upper 79.27; lower 74.50 | Bands narrowing; watch 74.50 |
| ATR | Volatility contracting | 1.70, down from ~2.20 on 2026-06-05 | Use ~1.7 points/day for sizing |
| VWMA | Price below | 76.84; falling since early June | Volume not yet confirming a reversal |
| Volume | Light on down day | 12.4M vs 17.1M average on 2026-07-06 | Breakdown not yet on heavy volume |
| Relative (20 sessions) | Underperforming | -0.36% vs +2.24% for ^BVSP (-2.60 pts) | Relative momentum is negative |
| Relative (120 sessions) | Slight underperformance | +4.11% vs +5.56% | Longer-term relative edge is modest |
| Beta / correlation | Tracks index | Beta 0.99; correlation 0.62 | Index-relative outcome depends on stock-specific news |
| Bull trigger | Reclaim 10 EMA and 76.9 | Close above 76.36–76.89 with volume | Would improve the relative case |
| Bear trigger | Close below ~75.6 cluster | Closes 75.58 (06-10), 75.61 (06-24) | Opens path toward 74.50 and 72.40 |
| Overall tilt | Neutral to slightly bearish (relative) | Combined evidence above | Wait for confirmation; size to ATR |

# VALE3.SA: Market Research Report (as of 2026-07-06)

## Bottom line

The evidence I could gather does not support a strong directional call on VALE3.SA relative to Ibovespa over the next 20 trading days. The main near-term catalyst is governance, not fundamentals: a board chair resignation today, a contested extraordinary shareholder meeting on 2026-07-22, and Q2 2026 results due in the same window. Brazil's macro backdrop has turned less supportive (higher rates, rising inflation, a weaker real). I would lean neutral, with event risk skewed to the downside until the board situation is clearer. This is a judgment from thin data, not a high-conviction view.

## Data limitations

- **Company news:** The news tool returned only CVM regulatory filings (type and subject, no content). I could not read the substance of the governance disclosures or any press coverage.
- **Global news:** The Yahoo Finance feed was unavailable for the window, so I have no US, China, or commodity headlines for the past week.
- **Prediction markets:** Odds for iron ore and China stimulus were withheld because the tool serves only live odds with no historical vintage, which would leak post-decision information into this analysis.
- **Prices:** I have no price or total-return data for VALE3.SA or ^BVSP, so I cannot assess momentum, valuation, or relative performance.

## 1. Company-specific: governance is the dominant story

Recent CVM filings show an active boardroom dispute:

- **2026-07-06:** Material fact on the resignation of the board chair. This is the most recent and most market-relevant item.
- **2026-06-24:** Company clarification of press reports ("Esclarecimento de notícias de imprensa"). The subject suggests the press was running stories the company felt needed correcting, but the content is not visible to me.
- **2026-06-24 / 06-23 / 06-19:** Board minutes and calls for an Extraordinary General Meeting on **2026-07-22**. The agenda covers removing director Daniel André Stieler, electing a new director, and electing a new board chair. Candidates named include Manuel Lino Silva de Sousa Oliveira and Marcelo Gasparino da Silva for chair.
- **2026-06-11:** Material fact on correspondence received from shareholder **Previ** (a major Brazilian pension fund and Vale shareholder). The subject line is all I have.

Read together, a large shareholder appears to be pressing on board composition, and the chair has now left. Governance contests at Brazilian large caps often lead to short-term volatility, sometimes a discount on the stock, and sometimes a re-rating if the outcome is seen as improving governance. Which direction applies here depends on content I cannot see. Traders should read the Previ letter, the 06-24 clarification, and today's material fact directly before sizing a position.

Other items:

- **2026-07-02:** The company disclosed its 2T26 (Q2 2026) results release dates. The results will likely fall inside the 20-day holding window, which adds earnings-driven volatility on top of the governance risk. I do not have the exact date from the filing content.
- **2026-06-15:** ISSB-standard sustainability report and ESG webinar (06-30). These are routine and unlikely to move the stock.
- **Governance policy re-filings (06-29):** Routine re-deliveries of corporate, risk, water, and tax-compliance policies. Not market-moving on their own.

## 2. Brazil macro: tightening backdrop

Data from Banco Central do Brasil:

| Indicator | Latest | Trend | Read-across |
|---|---|---|---|
| Selic target | 14.25% (2026-07-06) | Cut from 15.00% in January, in steps (14.75 → 14.50 → 14.25) | Still very restrictive. The easing cycle is shallow and slowing. |
| Focus median, end-2026 Selic | 14.00% (survey 2026-07-03) | Up from 12.25% in January, rising almost every week since mid-April | The market has pushed back its easing expectations sharply. Rates may stay higher for longer. |
| Focus median, end-2027 Selic | 12.00% | Std dev about 1.0 | Expectations for 2027 are more dispersed. |
| IPCA 12-month inflation | 4.72% (May 2026 print) | Up from 3.81% in February | Inflation has reaccelerated for three straight prints, which is the main reason the easing outlook has shifted. |
| USD/BRL (PTAX) | 5.167 (2026-07-06) | Up from 4.99 at end-April and 5.06 at end-May | The real has weakened about 3.5% since April. |

**Implications for VALE3.SA:**

- Vale earns in US dollars, so a weaker real raises its BRL-denominated revenue. This is a modest tailwind.
- Higher-for-longer Selic is a headwind for equity valuations generally and for the broader Ibovespa. Because the question is performance relative to ^BVSP, the rate effect on the index largely cancels out for a single stock unless VALE3.SA is more rate-sensitive than the index. Vale is an exporter and commodity producer, so its rate sensitivity is different from domestic-facing stocks, not clearly higher.
- The FX move helps Vale relative to domestic names, which is a potential relative-performance argument, but it is small and already partly visible in the 3.5% move since April.

## 3. Global and commodity context

I could not retrieve the past week's global news, and prediction-market odds on iron ore and China stimulus were withheld. The commodity case for Vale (iron ore prices and Chinese steel demand, which drive most of its earnings) is therefore unverified in this report. Another agent with access to commodity price data or current news should check iron ore prices, China property and stimulus news, and Vale's Q2 production and guidance expectations before any position is taken.

## 4. Scenario framing for the 20-day horizon

- **Upside case:** Governance dispute resolves constructively before or at the 07-22 meeting (for example, a negotiated board slate), Q2 results beat, and the real stays weak. Relative outperformance is plausible.
- **Downside case:** Contest escalates (Previ pushes for changes that the market reads as value-destructive or as instability), the chair vacancy persists into the meeting, or Q2 disappoints on production or costs. Underperformance is plausible, and a governance discount could widen.
- **Base case:** Noise around the meeting and results with no clear resolution inside the window. Relative performance close to flat, with higher volatility than usual.

## 5. Recommendation

- **Stance:** Neutral to slightly cautious on a relative basis for the 20-session window ending about four weeks from the first close after 2026-07-06.
- **Reasons:** Governance uncertainty concentrated in the holding window, the Q2 results event, and a tighter Brazil rate backdrop, partly offset by FX support.
- **Before acting:** Read the full text of the 06-11 Previ letter, the 06-24 press clarification, and the 07-06 material fact. Confirm the Q2 results date. Check current iron ore and China data. Obtain VALE3.SA and ^BVSP price data to assess how much governance risk is already priced in.
- **Sizing:** If holding or entering, keep position size modest and consider defining the risk around the 07-22 meeting date.

## Summary table

| Area | Key fact | Date / source | Signal for VALE3.SA (20-day horizon) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Board governance | Board chair resigned | 2026-07-06, material fact | Negative near-term uncertainty |
| Shareholder pressure | Previ correspondence disclosed | 2026-06-11, material fact | Negative to neutral, content unknown |
| Press controversy | Company clarified press reports | 2026-06-24 | Unknown, content not visible |
| EGM | Board removal and election, 07-22 | Called 2026-06-19 to 06-24 | Key event inside the window |
| Q2 2026 results | Release dates disclosed | 2026-07-02 | Earnings volatility inside the window |
| Selic | 14.25%, down from 15.00% | BCB, 2026-07-06 | Mildly negative for market, neutral for Vale |
| Focus end-2026 Selic | 14.00%, up from 12.25% in January | BCB Focus, 2026-07-03 | Easing priced out, mildly negative for market |
| IPCA 12m | 4.72%, up from 3.81% | BCB, May 2026 print | Hawkish pressure, mildly negative for market |
| USD/BRL | 5.167, real weaker since April | BCB PTAX, 2026-07-06 | Positive for Vale's BRL earnings |
| Iron ore / China | Not verified (data withheld or unavailable) | n/a | Unknown, the key missing input |
| Overall call | Neutral to slightly cautious, relative to ^BVSP | This report | Low conviction, event-driven |

evidence.text:
# VALE3.SA Fundamental Analysis Report

**As of:** 2026-07-06
**Instrument:** VALE3.SA (VALE S.A., common shares, B3)
**Horizon:** About 20 trading days, relative to ^BVSP (Ibovespa total return)

## 1. Data Availability

Several tools returned restricted data for this date, so this report is weaker than usual on valuation and insider activity:

- **`get_fundamentals`: withheld.** The vendor only serves present-day values for profile, market cap, valuation multiples, 52-week range and TTM figures. These would leak post-decision information. I have no P/E, EV/EBITDA, dividend yield, market cap or price-level data.
- **`get_insider_transactions`: withheld.** The vendor dates trades by execution, not filing, so it cannot establish what was public on 2026-07-06.
- **Available:** CVM-filed quarterly balance sheet (Q2 2025 to Q1 2026), cash flow (YTD) and income statement (Q2 2025, Q3 2025, Q1 2026, and FY2025). All values are R$ millions, consolidated, as filed.

Because the income statement mixes quarters and full years, I have not computed Q4 2025 directly. Where I derive a Q4 figure by subtracting YTD from FY, I say so.

## 2. Income Statement Analysis

| Period | Revenue | Gross Profit | Gross Margin | EBIT (pre-fin.) | EBIT Margin | Net Income | Net Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q2 2025 | 49,807 | 15,386 | 30.9% | 10,983 | 22.1% | 12,187 | 24.5% |
| Q3 2025 | 56,701 | 20,624 | 36.4% | 16,084 | 28.4% | 14,671 | 25.9% |
| Q1 2026 | 48,680 | 16,257 | 33.4% | 12,668 | 26.0% | 10,199 | 20.9% |
| FY 2025 | 213,595 | 74,708 | 35.0% | 31,969 | 15.0% | 11,811 | 5.5% |

**Observations:**

- **Q1 2026 is the latest quarter.** Revenue was R$48.7bn, down about 14% from Q3 2025 (R$56.7bn) but roughly in line with Q2 2025 (R$49.8bn). Operating margin (26.0%) is near the 2025 quarterly high and well above the FY2025 average, so the core operation is still profitable.
- **FY2025 net income of R$11.8bn is far below the sum of the quarters I can see.** Q2 and Q3 alone produced R$26.9bn of net income. That implies Q4 2025 plus Q1 2025 combined was about **–R$15.0bn**. Q1 2025 is not in the dataset, so I cannot isolate Q4. The gap points to a large non-recurring charge in late 2025 (impairment, provision, or tax item) that the filing data does not explain. The full FY2025 EBIT of R$32.0bn, against about R$27bn for Q2 plus Q3 alone, is consistent with a heavy charge in the operating line as well (FY operating expenses were R$42.7bn, versus R$4.5bn in Q3).
- **Tax rate is volatile.** FY2025 effective tax was about 56% (R$14.9bn on R$26.7bn pre-tax). Q1 2026 was about 21% (R$2.7bn on R$12.9bn). Q3 2025 showed a small tax credit. Normalised earnings are hard to pin down from this data.
- **Financial result turned positive in Q1 2026** (+R$211m) after a FY2025 net finance cost of –R$5.3bn, which helps Q1 earnings quality.

## 3. Balance Sheet Analysis

| Metric | Q2 2025 | Q3 2025 | Q4 2025 | Q1 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total Assets | 493,226 | 484,953 | 476,094 | 457,173 |
| Current Assets | 95,964 | 87,682 | 100,645 | 87,427 |
| Current Liabilities | 78,962 | 70,860 | 87,320 | 70,512 |
| Non-Current Liabilities | 193,299 | 189,360 | 199,848 | 190,746 |
| Shareholders' Equity | 220,965 | 224,733 | 188,926 | 195,915 |
| Current Ratio | 1.22x | 1.24x | 1.15x | 1.24x |
| Total Liabilities / Equity | 1.23x | 1.16x | 1.52x | 1.33x |

**Observations:**

- **Equity fell about R$36bn from Q3 2025 to Q4 2025** (224.7 to 188.9), then recovered R$7bn in Q1 2026 (195.9). The Q4 drop is consistent with the late-2025 loss and possibly with distributions or OCI effects. The filings do not split these out.
- **Leverage rose through the end of 2025 and eased in Q1 2026.** Liabilities-to-equity was 1.52x at Dec 2025 and 1.33x at Mar 2026. Total assets fell about 4% over the period, mainly in non-current assets (375.4 to 369.7bn).
- **Liquidity is adequate.** Current ratio is about 1.2x and stable. Working capital is positive (about R$17bn at Q1 2026).
- **Debt detail is not broken out** in the data provided, so I cannot compute net debt or net debt/EBITDA reliably. This is a gap for any leverage-based view.

## 4. Cash Flow Analysis

| Period | Operating CF | Investing CF | Financing CF | Net Change in Cash | Derived FCF proxy (CFO + Investing) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 2025 (YTD) | 20,292 | –19,410 | 1,307 | –578 | 882 |
| 9M 2025 (YTD) | 34,020 | –26,196 | –3,957 | 720 | 7,824 |
| FY 2025 | 48,765 | –38,463 | 1,239 | 9,892 | 10,302 |
| Q1 2026 | 9,777 | –6,687 | –15,885 | –14,023 | 3,090 |

**Derived quarterly figures (YTD differences):**

- **Q3 2025:** CFO ~13.7bn, investing ~–6.8bn
- **Q4 2025:** CFO ~14.7bn, investing ~–12.3bn, financing ~+5.2bn

**Observations:**

- **Operating cash generation is solid.** FY2025 CFO was R$48.8bn, and Q1 2026 CFO of R$9.8bn is a healthy quarterly run-rate. CFO comfortably exceeds the accounting net income in 2025, which indicates non-cash charges drove much of the Q4 loss, not operating weakness.
- **Investment is heavy.** Investing outflows of R$38.5bn in FY2025 absorbed about 79% of CFO. Q4 2025 investing spiked to about R$12.3bn. The FCF proxy (CFO plus investing) was only R$10.3bn for FY2025, a thin cushion for shareholder returns.
- **Q1 2026 financing outflow of R$15.9bn** is large. It most likely reflects dividends or interest-on-capital payments, debt repayment, or both. The data does not split this, so I cannot confirm the cause. It is the main reason cash fell R$14bn in the quarter.
- **Q1 2026 FCF proxy is about R$3.1bn**, which is modest. Outflows exceeded inflows for the period.

## 5. Company Profile and Context

The company profile is withheld, so the following is contextual background, not data from the tools:

- Vale is a major global iron ore and nickel producer. Iron ore pricing (largely Chinese steel demand), BRL/USD moves, and Brazilian dam-safety and regulatory issues are the main drivers of its share price. None of these is quantified in the data I have.
- Earnings are commodity-linked and cyclical, so quarterly swings like the ones above are normal. Operating margins of 26% in Q1 2026 suggest prices and costs are currently supportive, but I cannot verify the iron ore price level from these tools.

## 6. Insider Activity

Not available for this date. I cannot tell whether recent insider buying or selling was public as of 2026-07-06. Please treat insider signals as an open gap.

## 7. Assessment and Trading Implications

**Strengths**
- Q1 2026 operating margin of 26% and positive financial result.
- Positive CFO of about R$49bn in FY2025 and R$9.8bn in Q1 2026.
- Liquidity is stable (current ratio ~1.2x) and leverage eased from its Dec 2025 peak.
- Equity recovered about R$7bn in Q1 2026.

**Risks and gaps**
- The late-2025 earnings collapse (implied Q4 2025 plus Q1 2025 net loss of about R$15bn) is unexplained by the data. It may be a one-off, but it may also signal impairments or recurring charges. This needs a check against the DFP notes.
- Q1 2026 financing outflow of R$15.9bn drained cash by R$14bn. If this is recurring distributions, it may limit future balance-sheet flexibility.
- Heavy capex (investing about 79% of CFO in FY2025) leaves a small free-cash cushion.
- Valuation, price momentum and insider data are unavailable, so I cannot judge whether the stock already reflects this profile.

**Net view for a ~4-week horizon vs. the Ibovespa:** The fundamentals are mixed. Operations are generating cash and Q1 2026 margins are strong, which supports the business. But the unexplained late-2025 loss, the large Q1 2026 cash outflow, and the lack of valuation or insider data give me no clear edge on relative performance over four weeks. Over this short horizon, the outcome will depend more on iron ore prices, BRL moves and market-wide flows than on these filings. **Stance: neutral.** A trader should only take a directional position after confirming the cause of the Q4 2025 charge and the composition of the Q1 2026 financing outflow, and after checking current price and valuation from a source that is not restricted for this date.

## Key Points Summary

| Category | Metric / Finding | Value / Detail | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Q1 2026 revenue | R$48.7bn (–14% QoQ vs Q3 2025) | Neutral |
| Revenue | FY2025 revenue | R$213.6bn | Context |
| Margins | Q1 2026 gross / EBIT / net margin | 33.4% / 26.0% / 20.9% | Positive |
| Earnings | FY2025 net income | R$11.8bn (5.5% margin) | Negative (depressed by Q4) |
| Earnings | Implied Q4 2025 + Q1 2025 net loss | about –R$15.0bn (derived; unexplained) | Negative / needs review |
| Tax | FY2025 effective tax rate | ~56% | Negative / volatile |
| Tax | Q1 2026 effective tax rate | ~21% | Positive |
| Finance | Q1 2026 financial result | +R$0.2bn (vs –R$5.3bn FY2025) | Positive |

deliberation.title: Investment debate (bull and bear)
deliberation.text:
Bull Analyst: # Bull Case for VALE3.SA: 4-Week Relative Return vs. ^BVSP

**Opening position:** I'm recommending a modest long in VALE3.SA for the 20-session window after the 2026-07-07 close, with a clear invalidation level. I'm not claiming high conviction. The bull case rests on three things: the price is sitting on a demonstrated support zone, the selling lacks conviction, and the binary governance event is more likely to resolve than to escalate. Bears will say that is a lot to hang on a neutral data set. I think the setup is better than the headline numbers suggest.

## The chart is at a decision point, not a breakdown

The bears will point to the falling 50 SMA (80.52 to 78.72), the price below the 10 EMA, and MACD at -0.88. All true. But look at what the price is doing. VALE3.SA has closed at 75.58, 75.61, and now 75.67 on three separate dates, spread across roughly a month. That cluster has held. A stock that has tested the same level three times without breaking it is building a base, not rolling over.

The volume detail matters too. Today's 1.3% decline came on 12.4M shares, about 72% of the 20-session average. Distribution usually shows up as heavy volume on down days. Light volume on a down day says the sellers aren't pressing. The bears call this "not yet capitulation." I'd call it the absence of a forced seller.

Long-term structure is still intact. The 200 SMA has risen from 66.58 in early May to 72.40, and the price sits about 4.5% above it. Over 60 sessions VALE3.SA actually beat the index (-9.1% vs. -10.3%). The March–April drawdown is the real drag, not the recent tape.

## The momentum indicators are early, not terminal

RSI at 41.7 is not oversold, and the bears are right that there is no mean-reversion trigger yet. But the MACD histogram has shrunk to -0.011. Bearish momentum is fading. The useful question is not whether the indicators are bullish today. It is whether the path from here is more likely up or down. Compression in both ATR (from ~2.2 to 1.7) and Bollinger bandwidth often precedes expansion, and the Bollinger middle at 76.89 is only about 1.6% overhead. A reclaim of 76.4–76.9 on volume would flip the short-term structure with a small move.

## Governance: the bears are treating a catalyst as a verdict

This is where I expect the bear to press hardest. A chair resignation today, a contested EGM on 2026-07-22, and a Previ letter read as pressure on the board. The bear sees instability and a governance discount.

I see a process that is coming to a head. Contests like this tend to resolve one of two ways: a negotiated board slate that removes the uncertainty, or a vote that settles who runs the company. Either outcome removes an overhang. The market has a known date and the uncertainty is concentrated in one event. Markets generally price known binary events in advance, so the discount may already be partly in the 75–76 zone. I can't verify that from the data, and I'll concede it. But the bear's downside case assumes escalation. The more common endpoint for shareholder-driven governance disputes at large caps is a settlement, and settlements can produce a re-rating if investors see governance improving.

## Fundamentals: the bears are reading the 2025 charge as the present

The bear will cite the implied ~R$15bn loss across Q1 2025 and Q4 2025 and the equity drop of about R$36bn in Q4. Those are real and need answers. But they're backward-looking. Look at what came after:

- **Q1 2026 EBIT margin of 26.0%**, near the 2025 quarterly high. The core operation is earning well.
- **Financial result turned positive** (+R$0.2bn in Q1 2026 vs. –R$5.3bn for FY2025).
- **Operating cash flow of R$9.8bn in Q1 2026**, and R$48.8bn for FY2025. CFO well above accounting earnings suggests the 2025 loss was largely non-cash.
- **Leverage eased** from 1.52x liabilities-to-equity at December to 1.33x in March, and equity recovered about R$7bn.

The Q1 2026 financing outflow of R$15.9bn is the bear's best point, and I won't dismiss it. It may be dividends or interest on capital, which would be a shareholder-positive use of cash, or it may be debt repayment, which would be balance-sheet-positive. Either way it's a reason to check the cash flow statement, not a reason to assume distress.

## Macro: the FX tailwind is real even if the rate effect washes out

The bear is right that higher-for-longer Selic hits the index broadly. For a single stock measured against the Ibovespa, that effect largely cancels. But VALE3.SA earns in dollars. The real has weakened about 3.5% since April (USD/BRL 5.167), which lifts its BRL-denominated revenue relative to domestic names. That's a relative-performance argument the bears have to answer, and they can't dismiss it as noise when the stock's earnings base is in USD.

## Where the bears are right, and what I'd do about it

I'll concede three things. The iron ore and China demand picture is unverified, and that is the largest driver of Vale's earnings. The governance direction depends on content I haven't read. And the valuation data is missing, so I can't say how much of the positive view is already priced in.

Those gaps argue for sizing, not for abstaining. My plan:

- **Entry:** 2026-07-07 close (the horizon's reference).
- **Risk reference:** 1 ATR below entry, about 74.0. A close below the 74.50 lower Bollinger band would be the first warning. A close below 72.4 (the 200 SMA) would invalidate the long-term thesis.
- **Upside confirmation:** A daily close above 76.4–76.9 on above-average volume, and MACD histogram turning positive.
- **Event handling:** Keep the position modest into 07-22. Consider reducing if the EGM escalates without a negotiated outcome.

## Bottom line

The bear wants you to see a stock in trouble: a falling 50 SMA, a governance fight, an unexplained 2025 loss, and a tight rate backdrop. The data also shows a stock that has held a support zone three times, is selling on light volume, is still above a rising 200-day average, is posting strong operating margins, and is benefiting from a weaker real. The governance fight has a date attached and is more likely to resolve than to deepen.

I'd call that a modest long with a defined stop, not a conviction trade. The bear's strongest argument is that we don't yet know the iron ore price or the valuation. The honest answer is to size for that uncertainty. It isn't a reason to assume the outcome will be negative.
Bear Analyst: # Bear Case for VALE3.SA: Why the Long Doesn't Hold Up Against ^BVSP

My colleague's case reads like a case for a bottom. I think it's a case for waiting. The bull has built a long on three pillars: a support zone that's held, selling that lacks conviction, and a governance fight that will resolve cleanly. Each pillar is weaker than it looks, and together they don't give you an edge against the index over 20 sessions.

## The "support zone" is a ceiling in disguise

The bull says VALE3.SA has closed at 75.58, 75.61, and 75.67 on three dates, so the level has held. But three closes within 0.1 points of each other are a tight range, not a foundation. And repeated tests of a level usually weaken it. Each visit draws more sellers who were waiting to get out near that price.

Look at the volume-weighted average. The VWMA is 76.84, and the price is 1.5% below it. The VWMA has fallen from 80.46 since June 1, so the recent volume-weighted cost basis of holders sits above the current price. Those holders are underwater. Anyone who bought in the 76–80 zone will be looking to sell into any rally toward 76.8, which is exactly where the bull wants to buy confirmation.

The bull's own risk reference undercuts the thesis. If 75–76 is real support, a stop should sit just below it. Instead the bull proposes a stop at about 74.0, a level 2.2% below entry. On a crude random-walk scaling, with the ATR at 1.7 points and a 20-session spread of roughly ±7–8 points, a stop 2% away gets touched most of the time from noise alone. The bull has chosen a stop that the stock's ordinary movement will likely hit, and then calls the position "defined."

## Light volume on a down day isn't proof of a seller's absence

The bull calls the 12.4M-share decline "the absence of a forced seller." But the 20-session average is 17.1M, and that average includes the heavier selling from June. Volume falling below average on a down day can just as easily mean buyers have stepped back. Without a rise in volume on up days, there's no evidence of accumulation. The up days are also the ones to check, and the bull doesn't mention them.

## The long-term trend is intact, but the recent relative tape is not

The bull says VALE3.SA beat the index over 60 sessions (-9.1% vs. -10.3%) and that the March–April drawdown is the real drag. Look at the full table. Over 20 sessions, VALE3.SA trails ^BVSP by 2.6 points (-0.36% vs. +2.24%). Over 120 sessions it trails by 1.45 points. The 60-session "outperformance" is a rebound comparison from a trough, not a sign of current strength. For a four-week relative call, the most recent 20 sessions are the window that matters, and they point the wrong way.

The 200 SMA is rising, but it's a lagging average, and the price has already fallen from roughly 87.6 in February to 75.7. The cushion above the 200 SMA has shrunk to 4.5%, and at 0.12–0.15 points per session the average is catching up with the price, not pulling it higher.

## "Compression precedes expansion" is direction-neutral

The bull reads the shrinking histogram (-0.011), narrowing ATR, and tighter Bollinger bands as bullish. Compression tells you the next move will be larger. It doesn't tell you which way. And the MACD line is still below its signal line (-0.883 vs. -0.873). The bull also says the 76.4–76.9 reclaim is "a small move," but the real hurdle is the 50 SMA at 78.72, which is falling. Recent rallies have failed at 78.21 on the 10 EMA and at 49 on RSI in late June. The failed push toward 50 on RSI is a sign of sellers in control, not a setup that's about to flip.

## Governance: the bull is betting on the outcome he admits he hasn't read

The bull says contests "tend to resolve" through settlement, which removes the overhang. That's one possible path, and the bull assumes it's the likely one without evidence. Look at what the filings actually show:

- The board chair resigned today.
- The company had to issue a clarification on press reports on June 24, which means the story is already in the press in a form the company felt needed correcting.
- A pension fund shareholder, Previ, pressed the board, and the company disclosed that correspondence.
- An EGM on July 22 proposes removing a director and electing a new chair.

That's not a dispute winding down. The chair's departure leaves a leadership vacuum right before the vote that will decide the board. The bull's claim that the discount "may already be partly in the 75–76 zone" is an assumption, and the bull concedes he can't verify it. He's also building the long on an event whose content he hasn't read.

The timing is the bigger problem. The EGM (July 22) and the Q2 2026 results both fall inside the 20-session window. That's two binary events stacked in the period you're being asked to be long. For a relative-return bet, that's variance you're taking on without an edge in either direction.

## The fundamentals don't say what the bull says they say

**"The 2025 charge is backward-looking."** The data shows an implied net loss of about R$15bn across Q1 and Q4 2025 that nobody has explained, a R$36bn equity drop in Q4, and a 56% effective tax rate for FY2025. Those aren't a footnote. Until the cause is identified, the bull can't tell you it was one-off.

**"Q1 2026 margins are near the 2025 high."** Q1 2026 EBIT margin is 26.0%. Q3 2025 was 28.4%. Gross margin fell from 36.4% to 33.4%, and net margin from 25.9% to 20.9%. Revenue dropped 14% from Q3. Margins are compressing from their peak, not holding near it.

**"Leverage eased from the December peak."** Liabilities-to-equity is 1.33x. That's better than December's 1.52x, but still well above 1.16x in Q3 2025. The balance sheet is weaker than it was six months ago, and the equity recovery of about R$7bn only closes part of the gap. Equity is still around R$29bn below its September level.

**"The R$15.9bn financing outflow is either shareholder-positive or balance-sheet-positive."** Both options consume cash. If it was dividends, the payout was roughly five times the Q1 FCF proxy of R$3.1bn. If it was debt repayment, the money is gone, and the company is worth less cash than it was. Either way, cash fell R$14bn in a single quarter, and the free-cash cushion is thin. The bull presents a cash drain as a positive in both cases, which is a false choice. And who controls capital allocation is precisely what the board fight is about. The bull is asking you to ignore that link.

## The FX tailwind is real, but it's the same story that's hurting the market

The bull is right that a weaker real lifts Vale's BRL earnings. But the real has weakened about 3.5% since April because inflation is re-accelerating (IPCA 4.72%, up from 3.81%) and the market has priced out rate cuts (end-2026 Selic expectation of 14.00%, up from 12.25% in January). That's a risk-off backdrop for Brazilian assets in general. The FX gain is a partial offset to a broader pressure that could weigh on foreign flows into the index. For a relative bet, you'd need the stock to hold up better than the market in a tightening environment, and nothing in the data shows that.

## Where the bull is right, and why that doesn't save the trade

The bull concedes the three things that matter most: iron ore and China demand are unverified, the governance direction depends on content nobody has read, and valuation data is missing. He then argues that these gaps call for sizing, not abstaining.

I'd turn that around. A long decision should rest on an edge. The bull has no verified edge on the largest driver of Vale's earnings, no read on the event that will dominate the window, and no valuation to say whether good news is priced in. He's proposing to take the position anyway and manage it with a stop that sits inside normal noise. Smaller size doesn't fix a missing edge. It just makes a loss slower.

Note also that the bull never states a price target. Without one, the reward side is undefined. The most the bull can point to is a reclaim of the 50 SMA at 78.72, about 4% above entry, against a stop that's likely to be hit. That's not an attractive asymmetry.

## What I'd do instead

**Stance:** Avoid a long against ^BVSP for the 20-session window. If you're underweight the name, the case is strongest now. Being neutral-to-underweight is defensible. Being long is not.

**What would change my mind:**
- A daily close above the 50 SMA (78.72) on above-average volume, with MACD back above zero.
- A reading of the Previ letter and the July 6 material fact that shows a negotiated board slate, not a contested vote.
- A confirmed explanation for the 2025 loss and the Q1 2026 financing outflow.
- Iron ore and China data showing demand holding up.

**What would confirm the bear case:** A daily close below 75.5 on rising volume, which opens a move toward the lower Bollinger band at 74.50 and then the 200 SMA at 72.40. A chair vacancy that persists into July 22, or Q2 results that disappoint on production or cost, would add to that.

The bull wants you to believe a stock that's falling, in a governance fight, with an unexplained loss and rising rates, has found a floor. The evidence says it has found a ceiling at 76–77, and it hasn't yet shown that the buyers are back. Until it does, the four-week relative bet is one you don't have an edge on, and the stop the bull proposes is one you're likely to hit.

deliberation.title: Research manager's plan
deliberation.text:
**Recommendation**: Underweight

**Rationale**: Both sides agree the data is thin on the biggest drivers (iron ore/China, valuation, content of the governance filings), so neither has a verified fundamental edge. The call therefore rests on what is observable for a 20-session relative return versus ^BVSP. The bull's support-zone argument is weaker than presented: price sits below a falling VWMA (76.84), the 10 EMA and a falling 50 SMA (78.72), the MACD line is still below its signal, and rallies have stalled near 49 RSI and the 10 EMA. VALE3.SA trails ^BVSP over the last 20 sessions (-0.36% vs +2.24%). The 60-session outperformance is a rebound from a trough. The bull's compression-precedes-expansion point is direction-neutral. Light volume on a down day is ambiguous. The bull's 74.0 stop is also tight relative to normal 20-day variance. Two binary events fall inside the window: the 07-22 EGM, with the chair having resigned and Previ pressing the board, and Q2 results. That adds variance with no demonstrated edge, and a leadership vacuum makes escalation at least as plausible as settlement. Fundamentals are mixed. Q1 2026 margins are off the Q3 2025 peak (EBIT 26.0% vs 28.4%), liabilities-to-equity is better than December but worse than Q3 2025, the 2025 loss is unexplained, and cash fell sharply in Q1. The FX tailwind from a weaker real is real but modest and partly offset by the risk-off macro (rising IPCA, higher expected Selic). The bear's case is stronger on balance, but not decisively, since the price is above a rising 200 SMA and a negotiated governance outcome could re-rate the stock. That supports a modest underweight rather than a Sell.

**Strategic Actions**: Trim VALE3.SA to roughly 70-75% of a standard allocation relative to ^BVSP weight, or stay underweight if already below. Do not add before the 07-22 EGM. Scale the trim: do part now at the 07-07 close and hold the rest in reserve to trim on any bounce toward 76.4-76.9, which is the VWMA and Bollinger mid resistance zone. Confirmation of the bear case is a daily close below 75.5 on rising volume, which targets the 74.50 lower band and then the 200 SMA at 72.40. If that happens, consider deepening the underweight. Reverse toward neutral if there is a close above the 50 SMA (78.72) on above-average volume with MACD turning positive, or if filings show a negotiated board slate. Read the Previ letter and July 6 material fact, and check the cause of the 2025 loss and the Q1 financing outflow, before the EGM. Also check iron ore and China data, since none of this is verified here. Reassess around Q2 results and keep the position small enough that an EGM surprise in either direction is tolerable.

deliberation.title: Risk team debate
deliberation.text:
Aggressive Analyst: Let me open this, because the case for selling VALE3.SA is stronger than the trader's modest trim suggests. The trader is right about the direction but too timid about the size and the timing.

Start with the price structure. VALE3.SA closed at 75.67, below a 50-day average that is still falling at 78.72, below the 10-day EMA at 76.36, and below the Bollinger middle at 76.89. MACD is negative and sitting under its signal line. Over the last 20 sessions the stock is down 0.36% while Ibovespa is up 2.24%. That is a 2.6-point relative loss in a month when the market rose. The stock is not just lagging. It is losing relative strength while the index works in its favor, and that is the signal a relative-return trade should exploit.

Now the event calendar. The board chair resigned today, which is a material fact. A contested extraordinary meeting on July 22 will vote on removing a director and electing a new board chair, and Previ, a major pension fund shareholder, has been pressing the company since June. Q2 results land inside the same window. That is three negative-skew catalysts stacked in one 20-session window, and the company is not in a position of strength. The conservative voice will say we don't know what Previ's letter says, so we can't know the direction of the governance story. That's true, but it's the wrong conclusion. Unknown content in a boardroom fight with a chair walking out the door is not neutral. Markets price instability first and sort out the details later, and the sell-side and index flows usually take the first leg down before anyone reads the fine print.

The conservative analyst will also argue that the real's 3.5% slide since April is a tailwind for Vale's dollar revenue and should support the stock. I'd answer that it's already in the price, which has been flat-to-down through that same period. A currency tailwind that the stock can't convert into relative strength is a warning, not a cushion. And the neutral analyst will point out that the 200-day average at 72.40 is rising and the stock sits above it, so the long-term trend is intact. Fine, but the trade is a four-week relative call, not a bet on the next two years. A rising 200-day average is about 4 percent below the current price. That is the target zone, not a reason to stay out.

On the stop: the proposed 77.4 stop is about 2.3 percent above entry, or roughly 1.4 times the daily ATR of 1.7. That is tight, and in a stock with a governance headline, a single bad day could hit it without any thesis failure. But that's exactly why the sizing should be disciplined, not timid. If the thesis is right, the reward to a 72.4 to 74.5 move is roughly two to four times the risk. A position sized so a stop-out costs little, with room to add on confirmation, gives you the asymmetry you want.

On the trader's plan, I'd push harder. Holding back until the price bounces to 76.4 to 76.9 means waiting for the exact resistance zone where sellers have been defending, and it means you may never get filled if the stock gaps on the chair news. I would take a meaningful underweight now, at the top of the trim range, and treat any bounce toward the 10-day and Bollinger middle as an add opportunity rather than a reason to pare. Do not wait for the July 22 meeting to be resolved before acting. The skew is negative now, and the market will be reacting to headlines before the vote.

The honest risk is a governance resolution that the market reads as constructive, or a stronger-than-expected Q2 that squeezes shorts. Both are real. But you're not being paid to avoid volatility in a stock that is losing relative strength into a governance crisis. You're being paid to take the side of the trend while the crowd is still debating what the letter means.
Conservative Analyst: I'll start with what the aggressive case gets right. The technical picture is weak in the short and intermediate term, the chair resignation is a real event, and the July 22 meeting and Q2 results do fall inside the window. Where I part ways is on the leap from "the picture is weak" to "sell harder now, and add on any bounce." That leap depends on reading more into the data than it supports.

Take the relative-strength claim first. The 20-session gap is -2.6 points, but the same table shows VALE3.SA outperforming ^BVSP over 60 sessions by about 1.2 points and trailing by only 1.5 points over 120. The 5-session numbers are identical. With a 0.62 correlation to the index, a one-month relative gap is well within normal noise for this stock. Calling it a signal that a relative-return trade should exploit means treating a single window as a trend. A conservative desk doesn't stake capital on that.

The aggressive analyst also says the market will "take the first leg down" on governance headlines. But the one real piece of evidence we have contradicts that. The stock fell 1.33% on the day of the chair resignation, on 12.4 million shares against a 17.1 million average. That is a modest reaction on light volume, not a panic. We don't know what Previ's letter says, and that uncertainty is exactly why the position should be smaller, not larger. The aggressive analyst is right that unknown content isn't neutral, but the fact that it cuts both ways is the point. A contested meeting can end with a board slate the market reads as cleaner governance, and that can produce a sharp upside gap. Being short into that binary outcome is gap risk with a limited payoff.

The reward-to-risk math doesn't hold up either. Against the 77.4 stop, which is about 1.7 points above the 75.67 entry, the 74.5 lower Bollinger band is only about 1.2 points below. That's roughly 0.7 to 1, not the "two to four times" the aggressive analyst claimed. Only the 72.4 level gives close to 2 to 1, and reaching it means a 4.3% fall in a stock whose 20-session return is essentially flat. There's also a timing problem with that 72.4 target. The 200-day average has been rising about 0.12 to 0.15 points a session, so by the July exit date it will have climbed to roughly 75. The "target zone" is moving toward the current price, which means the cushion the aggressive analyst is counting on is shrinking as the trade ages.

On the currency argument, the aggressive analyst is right that the stock hasn't converted the weaker real into relative strength, and that is worth noting. But the inference that the FX tailwind is therefore a warning overreaches. A weaker real is a direct, known support for an exporter's BRL earnings, and it has been in place since April. The lack of a price response could reflect the governance discount, which is unknown in size, or it could reflect commodity pressure we can't see because the iron ore data was unavailable. Either way, that's a reason for humility about what the tape is telling us.

The most serious problem is the add-on-bounce advice. The aggressive analyst says to sell now, sell harder at the top of the trim range, and treat a bounce toward the 10-day EMA and Bollinger middle as an opportunity to add. Those levels, 76.36 and 76.89, are the exact bullish triggers the technical report lists as the first signs of repair. If the stock reclaims them on volume, the bearish thesis is being invalidated, and the plan is to add to the losing side. That is averaging into a position against the evidence, and it is how a manageable loss becomes a large one. The stop at 77.4 sits just above those levels, so the plan simultaneously calls the resistance decisive and tells you to keep adding into it.

The aggressive analyst also points to the short-squeeze risk and then dismisses it. A stronger-than-expected Q2 or a governance resolution that reads as constructive could push the stock sharply higher in a few sessions, and an underweight that was sized aggressively would absorb the full move. The fundamentals are also too unverified for conviction in either direction. The implied late-2025 loss is unexplained, the Q1 financing outflow of R$15.9 billion is unexplained, and valuation and insider data are missing. Those gaps argue against sizing up.

So my view is that the trader's plan is the more defensible one, with tighter discipline. Trim now to the 70 to 75 percent range, as proposed, and hold the remainder to trim into a bounce toward 76.4 to 76.9. Treat that bounce as a chance to reduce further, not a reason to add. Do not add before July 22, and let the stop at 77.4 define the exit if the bounce turns into a reclaim. Size the position so that a single gap through the stop on governance news costs a small, pre-defined fraction of the book, not a meaningful one. If the Previ letter or the Q2 date reveals something material, we can revisit the size then. Until then, the honest answer is that we have a weak trend, a binary event, and thin data, and the right response to all three is a smaller position, not a larger one.
Neutral Analyst: I think both of my colleagues have a point, and both overreach in ways that matter for a four-week call measured against ^BVSP.

Start with the aggressive case. Its strongest argument is the technical picture: the 50 SMA is falling and sits overhead, the price is below the 10 EMA and the Bollinger middle, and MACD is negative. Those facts justify leaning underweight. But the aggressive analyst then stacks a governance story on top and calls it three negative catalysts. That's not quite right. The Q2 results have no known direction. Q1 2026 showed a 26% operating margin, operating cash flow stayed strong, and a weaker real helps a dollar earner. Treating the results as a negative skew is an assumption, not something the data shows. The governance fight is also two-sided. A board chair leaving and a shareholder like Previ pressing could produce a worse board, or it could produce the cleaner governance that some investors have wanted. We don't know which, and the aggressive case quietly assumes the bad outcome.

The reward-to-risk math is also wrong. Against a 77.4 stop, the 74.5 Bollinger band is only about 0.7 times the risk, and even the 72.4 level is closer to 1.9 times. The "two to four times" figure doesn't survive the arithmetic. And the advice to add on a bounce into 76.4 to 76.9 is the part I'd most object to. Those are the exact levels that would signal trend repair. If the stock reclaims them on volume, the thesis is being challenged, and adding to the position means doubling down on the side the evidence is moving against.

The conservative case is right about the add-on problem and right that a one-month relative gap on a 0.62 correlation isn't much of a trend signal. But I think it leans too far the other way. Saying the trade is well within noise and the fundamentals are too unverified to act on is one thing. Concluding that we should barely act at all is another. The 20-session underperformance is -2.6 points, the price sits below every short-term average, and the 50 SMA is rolling over. Those are real signals even if they're not strong ones. Being too small can be as much a mistake as being too big, if the trend does break lower.

The conservative analyst also treats the FX tailwind as a plain support, but it's been present since April while the stock stayed flat to down. A tailwind the market isn't paying for is informative. It might be the governance discount, or commodity pressure, but either way the tape isn't rewarding it, and the conservative read should acknowledge that rather than explain it away.

Where I'd land is a moderate underweight that is explicitly relative to ^BVSP. One practical point: if you simply sell VALE3.SA into cash, you're taking on market direction that doesn't count toward a relative call. Framing it as an underweight versus the index weight keeps the bet aligned with how the outcome is measured. Sizing in the 70 to 75 percent range of standard allocation is a reasonable middle, and the 77.4 stop is defensible as a hard line, since a close above it would mean the setup has failed on the intermediate trend.

On the bounce, I'd change the rule. Don't add into 76.4 to 76.9, and don't simply hold either. If the stock closes back above the 10 EMA and the Bollinger middle on above-average volume, that's a reason to cut the underweight further toward flat, not to add. If the bounce fades on light volume below those levels, that's the case for holding the remainder. Pre-decide what you'll do at each level so you're not improvising on a gap.

The July 22 meeting is the harder question. Holding a meaningful underweight through a binary vote means accepting gap risk on a single day, and the stop at 77.4 may not protect you from an overnight move. I'd keep the position small enough that a gap through the stop costs a pre-set, acceptable fraction of the book. Whether to trim further ahead of the meeting depends on how much you trust the technical signal relative to the event risk, and that's a judgment the data can't settle.

Two data gaps are worth checking before you size up. First, confirm whether the price series is dividend-adjusted and whether an ex-dividend date falls in the window, since that changes how the total-return comparison works. Second, read the Previ letter and the Q2 date before the EGM. Those two items could move this call more than any chart signal, and the conservative analyst is right that they argue for keeping size modest until they're known.

So my view is a SELL as a partial, relative underweight, sized in the range the trader proposed, with a hard stop at 77.4, no adds into resistance, and a rule to reduce rather than add if the stock reclaims the short-term averages on volume. That keeps the trend view, limits the damage from a governance gap, and avoids betting big on a story whose direction nobody can yet see.
